Subject: Next steps: post-demo privacy items & erase-request orchestration

Hi Amelia / Nathan —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap plus a proposed set of next steps so we can line up the right folks on our side: you raised three core privacy/retention concerns I want to ensure we address explicitly: PII scoping (what we persist), deletion/erase request SLOs, and backup/residency constraints.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- PII: patient identifiers (MRNs) + free-text notes will be sent to Redwood for inference. Need deterministic controls to avoid storing raw PHI beyond request lifetime.
- Deletion / Right to be forgotten: ClearHealth needs the ability to fully erase a subject's data on request and receive confirmation. Target: 72 hours for primary stores; backups are a hard constraint — you asked whether backups can be shortened or excluded.
- Residency: Data must remain in-us (no eu/apac models or storage).
- Logging and audit: Immutable audit trail of delete requests and admin actions; redaction of logs that contain PII.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) Technical sync (SE + infra) to review how we do logical deletes, KV/prefix cache handling, and backup lifecycle (30/90 day scenarios). Marissa from our infra team suggested a 1-hour deep-dive.
2) Legal alignment: propose DPA amendment language and deletion SLA options; loop in Rishi.
3) Draft runbook: simple confirmation payload for each delete request + proof-of-deletion artifact (screenshot/ID and audit entry).

Action items for ClearHealth to help us scope:
- Confirm whether 72h primary-store SLO is firm or flexible to 7 days if backups require it.
- Confirm whether backups must be purged earlier than provider snapshot window or whether logical deletion + sealed backup window is acceptable.
- Share a redacted example of the objects/keys used (or schema) so Marissa can map retention paths.

I've attached a short spreadsheet of DPA questions and a diagram of a proposed erase orchestration for your review. Can we schedule the technical deep-dive Wednesday (US morning)?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0192

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the clear summary — that aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers to your action items:
- 72 hours for primary stores is our preference for patient-facing workflows; however, for lower-risk audit records 7 days is tolerable if you can get 72h for primary inference stores.
- Backups: our legal team is hesitant to accept a 30-day immutable window for backups unless we get a contractual guarantee about scope. Ideally, we can define a "backup carve-out" where product/metadata needed for system health is excluded from patient identifiers and can be retained longer. We want the actual PII not to survive in backups more than 30 days, if possible.
- I'll send a sanitized schema tomorrow (Nathan will follow up).

Yes to a technical deep-dive Wednesday morning PT. Please include your SE and anyone who can speak to snapshot/backup timelines.

Best,
Amelia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 08:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: post-demo privacy items & erase-request orchestration

Hi all —

Thanks Tessa — I dug into the attached questions and sketched two practical paths. High level answers to date-related questions:

1) Primary stores (index/kv/caches): we can implement a hard logical delete path that removes the object and associated KV cache within a job run; confirmation delivered via audit entry and a proof-of-deletion report. We can meet 72 hours for primary stores assuming timely request intake and no downstream third-party copy processes.

2) Backups / snapshot windows: public cloud snapshots are typically immutable until their retention window (30/60/90 days depending on customer settings). Options:
  - Default hosted: logical deletion in 72h + backups retained as per provider snapshot policy (default 30 days). We will add a DPA paragraph that limits backup scope: exclude patient-identifying fields from system-level snapshots via a transform pipeline (pseudonymize before snapshot) where feasible.
  - Dedicated / Private: with a dedicated pool or on-prem deployment we can reduce snapshot retention or run shorter snapshot cycles; we can also implement a policy to trigger immediate backup re-encryption + expunge metadata on request, then schedule physical purges on the next snapshot compaction. This typically requires a contractual SLA and an ops playbook.

3) Residency: we can restrict model and storage nodes to the us-region and verify with a signed attestation.

4) Logs: we can redact PII from operational logs and maintain an immutable audit of delete requests that references internal IDs (not raw PII).

5) Proof artifacts: we'll produce a proof-of-deletion JSON + signed audit entry for each request. If ClearHealth needs a human-readable certificate, we can add that as a deliverable.

Next: I recommend a quick tech run 45-min slot WED 10:30am PT where I can share an erase-workflow diagram and Rishi can talk to contract language. If ClearHealth confirms, I'll prepare two bullet lists for decision (hosted vs dedicated) and rough TCO delta.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Please send a short redline DPA amendment we can share with legal (we'll need the backup carve-out language included).
2) Provide an itemized list of deliverables and an estimated timeline (we'd like a formal runbook in the SOW and a DocuSign-ready statement of work).

If you can get the DPA amendment + SOW outline by end-of-day Thursday PT we'll aim to fast-track procurement next week. Once you share I will loop in procurement and our security reviewer.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Amelia
